extension.summary: View your Immich photos and videos in Kodi
extension.description: Browse the timeline, On this day, people and pets, places, albums and favourites of a self-hosted Immich server, or search by description. Watch them as a slideshow that crossfades and slowly pans and zooms across each photo, with photo details at the press of Info. View only: nothing is changed on the server. Menu tiles and photo backgrounds need Pillow in Kodi's Python; without it the plain photos are shown.
extension.disclaimer: Requires an Immich server that you own or have an account on. Not affiliated with the Immich project.
extension.news: v0.3.12 - Playing a video can no longer freeze Kodi for a minute v0.3.11 - Needs Kodi 22; a fanart for the add-on; debug lines only in Kodi's debug log v0.3.10 - A thinner outline behind the slideshow caption, date and clock - Kodi quits promptly even with a photo on its way through the proxy v0.3.9 - Folder backgrounds show the whole photo, on a blurred copy of itself, instead of a crop v0.3.8 - Years and months in Timeline, and countries in Places, show one of their photos v0.3.7 - Tile names are drawn properly with the Estuary skin's font v0.3.6 - Favourites that showed a tile go back to the Immich icon by themselves, keeping their place v0.3.5 - Tiles stay on the menu: Immich favourites no longer get one, so pick a thumbnail again for any that did - Kodi quits promptly even with a photo or tile request under way v0.3.4 - Kodi no longer waits long on a slow server when it quits while tiles are drawn v0.3.3 - Long tile names wrap onto two lines, so every name stays larger - Tiles redraw straight after an update v0.3.2 - Shuffle everything gets a photo tile too - A soft shadow keeps tile names readable on bright photos v0.3.1 - Photo tiles: the menu and Immich favourites show one of your photos with the folder's name, a new one each day - Rotated phone portraits zoom again on 4K screens v0.3.0 - Pausing eases the photo back to the whole picture and shows it at its sharpest - The caption, clock and Paused have an outline instead of a dark band along the screen edge
